content.comment_body: I've purchased [product_name] and installed the programming software on my computer. I'm new to PLC programming and need assistance. My work task is to set up a basic downtime capture system for a conveyor carrying products. I plan to use a sensor to detect when products are present. If the sensor isn't active (no product passing), I want to log this as downtime during the day. I also need to output these downtime records to a graph or spreadsheet so management can easily review the downtime for the day. Could someone provide guidance or programming help? Any advice would be appreciated. Thank you.

Are there any other conditions to consider? Just monitoring when the sensor is free might cause time outside normal shift hours to be counted. You could use the sensor signal together with the operation of the line. Should the time be tracked only during shift hours with counters resetting at shift end, or should tracking continue? Or do you need both a shift counter and a continuous counter? Where should the results be displayed?

Thank you for replying. Production runs from 7:00am to 12:00am, Monday through Friday. The counter needs to reset at midnight and restart at 7:00am the next day. At the end of each shift, I need to export the data to an Excel-compatible format for management to review downtime from the previous day. There's a brief 1-2 second gap between products on the conveyor, so I’d prefer downtime counting to start only after about 1 minute with no product detected—so a delay before logging downtime is needed. Any suggestion is welcome.

What degree of timing accuracy do you need—by seconds? That’s possible if specified. The latest [product_name] version features an enhanced web server. If integrated into your company's network, you can monitor current downtime in real time and view total times between shift transitions such as at 7:00am. Additionally, you can record the total time after each day in a DataLog.

Precision to the minute is sufficient. I haven’t wired or configured anything yet. For now, saving data to a DataLog file at the shift’s end should suffice. Is it possible to review this DataLog file in Excel and visualize it as a graph?
Here’s a short video showing the conveyor with products.
Yes, this is doable. It requires using a Micro SD card with [product_name].
Here is a suggestion for tracking downtime.

Is it possible for you to assist with writing the code needed for this process? As explained, I don’t have experience with coding but would like to simulate the solution in the software to learn. There’s no urgency—just whenever you have time. Thanks again for your support; it’s very helpful.
Apologies for just seeing your previous message. I’ll check the link you provided right away.
It seems our responses have overlapped.

Thank you for all the assistance. I hope to have time next week to install [product_name] and the sensor to test out the code. I’ll keep you updated on how it goes. Have a great weekend. Kindest Regards: [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A newcomer to [company_name] control hardware and programming tools is seeking advice for setting up a downtime monitoring system on a conveyor. Challenges include a lack of automation experience, the need for clear step-by-step programming support, timing accuracy, exporting shift data for managerial review, and simple methods for data visualization. Community replies clarified requirements and confirmed that features like data logging and export to Excel are feasible, though comprehensive beginner tutorials or templates seem unavailable.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants straightforward guidance for configuring [product_name] to log downtime accurately, reset counters at shift end, and export results in a format suitable for Excel. The solution should cater to beginners and require minimal PLC programming skills.
